newsitem.title: EGYPT: Computer problems send Cairo bourse sliding.
newsitem.headline: Computer problems send Cairo bourse sliding.

text.p: Computer problems returned on Wednesday to haunt the Egyptian stock exchange and pushed share prices a quarter of a percent lower, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index shed 1.25 points to 233.12 while turnover also fell to a below-average 14.94 million pounds ($4.39 million).
"Investors are selling, they're worried about this new system that keeps crashing and the clearing system as well," said broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB.
Brokers said trade transactions were being severely delayed by the clearing system, which stipulates that brokers must wrap up trades after a maximum of two days.

"But now when we do a buy transaction, we give the clearing house money and they don't give us our shares. Now we have no money to buy anything... this system must be fixed or else there will be a crisis," Khalil said.
The selling trend also hit the popular milling shares and prices were mostly lower. East Delta Flour Mills fell 0.38 pounds to 36.12 while Upper Egypt Flour Mills slipped 2.4 pounds to 46.1.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills, the day's most active share, was among the sector's few gainers and ended 0.15 to 52.5 pounds.

Trading on the bourse came to a complete standstill on Sunday after the computer system crashed and was restored five minutes before the end of the session. Technical problems from a new dealing system also hindered trade on the bourse on Monday.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell 4.45 points to 354.57 points, its lowest level in nearly a month, while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 162.88 from 163.62 on Tuesday.
